Optimise a function

Source: R/optimix.R
optimix.Rd

The single entry point. Pass a function with lower and upper bounds for the easy path, or a prepared optim_problem() for full control. With method = "auto" (the default) the best available optimiser is chosen for the problem and recorded in the result's provenance.

Usage

optimix(
  fn,
  lower = NULL,
  upper = NULL,
  ...,
  method = "auto",
  maximise = FALSE,
  max_evals = NULL,
  goal = c("optimum", "map")
)

minimise(fn, lower, upper, ...)

maximise(fn, lower, upper, ...)

Arguments

fn

The objective function, taking a numeric vector and returning a single finite number; or a prepared optim_problem(), in which case lower, upper, maximise, and max_evals are ignored.

lower

A numeric vector of lower bounds (easy path).

upper

A numeric vector of upper bounds (easy path).

...

Further arguments passed on to fn at each evaluation.

method

The optimiser to use: "auto" (the default) to select one per instance, "race" to race the installed global engines and commit to the leader, or the name of a registered engine (see list_optimisers()).

maximise

A single logical; maximise rather than minimise. Defaults to FALSE.

max_evals

A soft budget of objective evaluations, or NULL to let the engine use its own default.

goal

What to return: "optimum" (the default) for the single best point, or "map" for the full set of optima with a posterior over the optimum-set. goal = "map" steers method = "auto" to a map-emitting engine (proxymix's from_objective mixture); it is ignored when a specific method is named. For the richer queryable map object see optimix_map().

Value

An optimix_result: a list shaped like a stats::optim() result (par, value, counts, convergence, message) with optimix extras (provenance, map, diagnostics, problem). It has print(), summary(), plot(), coef(), as.data.frame(), and as_optim() methods. Results embed the problem, including the objective closure and its environment, and are therefore session objects; as_optim() gives the minimal durable form for storage.

See also

Other results: as_optim(), optimix_map()

Examples

# Easy path: minimise a quadratic on a box.
optimix(function(x) sum(x^2), lower = c(-5, -5), upper = c(5, 5),
        method = "base_optim")
#> <optimix_result>
#>   optimiser : base_optim
#>   value     : 0
#>   par       : 0, 0
#>   evals     : 5
#>   converged : yes

# Power path: a prepared problem.
prob <- optim_problem(
  fn = function(x) sum((x - 1)^2),
  space = space_box(lower = c(-5, -5), upper = c(5, 5))
)
optimix(prob, method = "base_optim")
#> <optimix_result>
#>   optimiser : base_optim
#>   value     : 0
#>   par       : 1, 1
#>   evals     : 20
#>   converged : yes
